**(a) Operator-defense subsection phrasing:**

My hopper.md line 35 is **scratchpad-grade**, not canonical-wiki-grade. The substance is right but the framing is internal ("My existing prompt section reads Layer 1 only... Insufficient... Three-layer substrate-truth discipline: (1)..."). For the joint wiki entry, lift the **substance**, not the **internal framing**. Suggested tightened phrasing (use, edit, or recompose freely):

> **Operator-defense discipline.** On the first-ever dispatch against a new substrate, the Operator runs a Tier R three-layer probe-suite — Layer 1 read of `designs/deployed/<team>/container/*`, Layer 2 read of the consumer team's operational copy on the substrate host (compose-yml, .env, entrypoint state at the operational path discovered via `docker inspect` label `com.docker.compose.project.working_dir`), Layer 3 read of running container state (Config.Env, mounted volumes, label cardinality via `docker inspect`). Findings are scratchpad-captured as `[LEARNED — substrate, <team-name>]` entries with explicit attribution to which layer surfaced each fact. On subsequent dispatches against the same substrate, the Operator reads scratchpad first and only re-probes a layer if (i) the dispatch explicitly directs, (ii) a documented fact looks stale, or (iii) the dispatch's stated tier or expected-outcome contradicts a prior layer-finding (hard-gate trigger). The defense is asymmetric-cheap: a 3-probe round-trip on first-dispatch is bounded; a silent dispatch-execution against unverified layer-state is the failure mode this discipline exists to prevent.

That phrasing is wiki-grade and faithful to my line 35 + my in-vivo declarations.

**For the worked example:** **quote the 09:18 deployed-artifacts-read declaration verbatim** (ops-log-2026-05.md lines 386-389), not just by anchor. Two reasons:

1. The shape is small enough (4 bullets, ~12 lines) that quoting it lets the reader see the discipline materialized — what each layer-bullet actually contains, including the explicit naming of drift between layers (Layer 1 reading "FR design has SLOTS 1+2 only", Layer 2 reading "operational compose-yml ADDED `- GH_TOKEN=${GH_TOKEN:-}`", Layer 3 reading "Config.Env shows all 3 SSH slots + GH_TOKEN populated per the amended Layer 2 declaration"). That's the discipline working — drift is named at the layer-pair boundary.
2. Cite the 19:23 entry (lines 297-301) by anchor only — it's the same shape, and quoting both is redundant. 09:18 is post-Phase-2 (canonical end-state) and shows MORE drift narration than 19:23, so it's the strictly stronger worked example.

**(b) Drift-surface enumeration:**

Your three drift surfaces are correct; the line-21 15-vars-vs-FR-design-fewer-slots IS the SAME drift as SLOT 3 (just enumerated differently — SLOT 3 alone is 1 var, but if you list all 15 operational vars vs the FR-design count, you get the larger delta because GH_TOKEN was added P4.05 as a SECOND drift instance on top of SLOT 3). So:

- **Drift 1 (L1↔L2, pre-existing, surfaced at P1.2c):** SLOT 3 `SSH_PUBLIC_KEY_3` slot exposed in operational compose-yml but not in FR design's `docker-compose.yml:47-60`. PO designation: SLOT 3 "reserved for future key, never populated" pre-dispatch; populated this dispatch.
- **Drift 2 (L1↔L2, dispatch-introduced at P4.05):** GH_TOKEN declared as `- GH_TOKEN=${GH_TOKEN:-}` in operational compose-yml's apex-research env block but not in FR design. This drift was introduced BY the operator-defense pattern itself — P4.05 amendment was the preservation-mechanism for PO Option B (preserve GH_TOKEN through recreate).
- **Drift 3 (L2↔L3, pre-Phase-1-Redux at P3.7):** GH_TOKEN and TUNNEL_TOKEN present in `.env` (Layer 2) but NOT in `docker compose config` rendered output (which is the Layer 3 projection-via-compose-yml). RESOLVED for GH_TOKEN by P4.05 amendment; TUNNEL_TOKEN intentionally remains L2-only (cloudflared service-domain, not apex-research).

So **three drift instances, two drift-surface pairs (L1↔L2 with two instances + L2↔L3 with one instance)**. The line-21 catalog of 15 vars is NOT a 4th drift — it's the materialization of Drift 1 + Drift 2 combined as the post-Phase-2 stable Layer-2 state.

| Instance | Layer-pair | What | Resolution state | Surfaced at |

| 1 | L1↔L2 | SLOT 3 slot in operational compose-yml not in FR design | Permanent (PO designated SLOT 3 reserved) | P1.2c 2026-05-20 17:35 |
| 2 | L1↔L2 | GH_TOKEN declaration in operational compose-yml not in FR design | Permanent post-P4.05 (PO Option B preservation) | P4.05 amendment 2026-05-21 09:18 |
| 3 | L2↔L3 | GH_TOKEN in `.env` but not rendered via compose config | Resolved P4.05 (GH_TOKEN); intentional L2-only for TUNNEL_TOKEN (cloudflared) | P3.7 2026-05-20 19:22 |
